checkpoints.note: The packet layer has already dispatched SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_REQUEST into ssh_packet_userauth_request, the initial sss unpack succeeded, and the parsed method string equals publickey. Control therefore enters the publickey-specific parser that consumes the remaining five payload bytes with ssh_buffer_unpack(packet, "bSS", ...).

First project-code parse inside the vulnerable userauth handler. It materializes the attacker-controlled method string and advances the packet cursor to the method-specific payload later consumed by the buggy bSS unpack.

Rollback of previously unpacked scalar outputs consumes va_arg(ap_copy, ...) only when buffer->secure is true. On the normal non-secure packet buffer this skips the leading 'b' argument &has_sign, leaves ap_copy misaligned, and causes the following 'S' cleanup to reinterpret &has_sign as ssh_string *. The fix moves the va_arg(ap_copy, ...) out of the if(buffer->secure) block for b/w/d/q so rollback always advances the copied va_list.

AddressSanitizer crash site. SAFE_FREE first evaluates *o.string as a pointer-sized value. Because rollback mis-set o.string to &has_sign, this dereference reads 8 bytes starting at the 1-byte has_sign stack object in ssh_packet_userauth_request, causing the observed stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 8.
